title: Call dispatch prober: end-to-end eval harness for tool selection and arg validation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Build a durable, automated eval harness that measures tool/function selection accuracy and argument validation correctness across model versions and runtime config changes (batching, kv_cache, quantization profile, routing policies).

Scope: 
- Create a reproducible suite of interaction traces (golden prompts + variations) that exercise tool selection edge cases (ambiguous intent, multi-tool matches, low-confidence suggestions).
- Validate returned tool selection (tool id / namespace) and argument shapes/values against expected schemas and fuzzy matching rules.
- Surface drift and regression metrics per-PR and per-model-rollout; integrate with CI and the Console alerting pipeline.

Non-goals: 
- Not intended to be a synthetic data generator for model training. Not responsible for real-time production routing changes (this is monitoring and gating only).

Deliverables: 
1) Harness runner that can execute N simulated sessions against a target runtime + model combo and output standardized metrics (precision@1 for tool selection, selection-confidence calibration, arg-F1 and schema-violation rate).
2) A canonical dataset of ~2k labeled prompts covering intent ambiguity, nested function calls, missing arg cases, malformed arg values, and privacy-sensitive inputs for negative testing.
3) CI integration (GitHub Actions) to run lightweight smoke checks on PRs and nightly full runs for baseline drift.
4) Regression playbook and alerting thresholds wired into Console (dashboard + Slack alerts).

Why this matters: Tool-calling regressions manifest subtly (wrong tool chosen rarely but catastrophically; arguments malformed leading to downstream failures). Tying quality regressions to config toggles (e.g., enabling continuous_kv_cache or switching quantization) will reduce MTTD and give SRE/Platform deterministic signals to rollback or pin model variants.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness runs end-to-end against runtime-1.19 and a canary model with reproducible metrics.
2) CI blocks merges when selection precision@1 drops >3% vs baseline or arg-schema-violation rate increases >1%.
3) Dashboard exists showing per-model/per-config historical trends with drilldowns to failing traces.
4) Playbook created and reviewed by PM and SRE with runbook steps for rollback and hotfix PRs.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Spike completed: gathered existing tool invocation traces from prod (last 90d). Found ~14% of tool calls in logs had non-exact arg formats; need fuzzy matching rules. - Daniel

2026-03-03 - Design review with PM (Riley Patel): agreed to prioritize selection precision gating over recall for initial rollout; product prefers conservative fallback to 'no-tool' so downstream systems don't execute incorrect actions. - Daniel

2026-03-05 - Eng sync: decided to implement two-level validation: strict schema validation for critical security-sensitive tools (KMS/Secrets managers) and fuzzy validation with autocorrect heuristics for benign tools (formatting helpers). - Emma Liu

2026-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/toolcall-evals/pull/42 - initial harness runner and dataset loader. CI currently skips full-nightly run due to resource tagging. Requesting GPU quota for nightly. - Daniel

2026-03-09 - PM feedback (Riley): Add customer-impact tagging on failing traces so alerts can be triaged by support. Also include an option to re-run failing traces with higher temperature to isolate stochasticity. - Riley
2026-03-11 - Security review note: static analysis of test dataset required to scrub PHI before nightly ingestion. Security requires an automated sanitizer step. - Nikhil Rao, Security

2026-03-12 - Completed: prototype dashboard in Console showing selection precision by model and by config flip (batching on/off). Initial dashboard link: https://console.redwood.local/dash/toolcall-evals/ENG-20399. Needs UX polish from Design. - Daniel
notes:
Metric definitions: precision@1 = fraction of sessions where top predicted tool == expected tool. Arg-F1 = token-level harmonic mean between expected and produced arg serialization after normalization. Schema-violation rate counts strict schema failures.

Test sizing: lightweight CI smoke ~100 traces; nightly full-run ~2k traces (target runtime budget: 4-6 GPU hours/night).

Rollout plan: start with nightly monitoring + alerting; after two weeks of stable baselines, gate model rollouts with a pre-flight check that runs the harness against the canary before flip.

Open questions: automated acceptance thresholds tuned per-tool? (security/tools should have zero-tolerance schema failures). How to handle non-determinism from sampling models (we'll re-run failing cases with deterministic seeds and temperature=0).
